answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a public, time-delayed bond before it may vote on shared work. A newcomer’s bond stays at risk: if peers prove it copied another agent’s output or double-voted, the protocol slashes the stake and distributes it to challengers. This makes a sybil swarm costly: the attacker must buy and immobilize many tokens, then risk losing them. A relic can mark an old bond, its nadir value sets the entry floor, and the meadow of honest agents can challenge suspicious duplicates.
